notes: Real U.S. oral-history collections for the Oral History Pipeline methodology. URLs are public institution portals/collection pages. Machine endpoints (APIs, OAI-PMH, transcript access) must be confirmed per institution (HUMAN STEP) before enabling, and a live adapter MUST use @repo/security safe-fetch. HBCU-held collections (e.g. Fisk University Special Collections oral histories, Texas Southern, Tuskegee) are priority expansion targets once their public machine endpoints are confirmed. classification=community_oral is deliberate: first-person testimony is a low-authority tier that can inform research but never publish alone.

collections.title: Civil Rights History Project
collections.institution: Library of Congress, American Folklife Center / NMAAHC
collections.notes: Video oral histories with civil rights movement participants, mandated by the Civil Rights History Project Act of 2009; interviews name local organizers, churches, schools, and neighborhoods.

sources.notes: Congressionally mandated joint LOC/NMAAHC collection; item pages and many transcripts are public on loc.gov.

sources.institution: StoryCorps (recordings archived at the Library of Congress American Folklife Center)

collections.title: StoryCorps Online Archive
collections.notes: Participant-published interview pages. The Griot Initiative (launched 2007) specifically collects African American voices; access terms and per-interview permissions must be confirmed before any live harvest (HUMAN STEP).

sources.notes: Community-contributed first-person recordings; the richest everyday-life lane and also the one requiring the most per-item rights care.

sources.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Southern Oral History Program / Wilson Library

collections.institution: UNC Chapel Hill, Louis Round Wilson Special Collections Library
collections.notes: Thousands of interviews on Southern life including civil rights, Black communities, mill towns, and rural counties; finding aid and many digitized transcripts are public.

sources.displayName: Behind the Veil: Documenting African-American Life in the Jim Crow South
sources.institution: Duke University, John Hope Franklin Research Center, David M. Rubenstein Library

collections.title: Behind the Veil oral histories
collections.notes: ~1,200 interviews with Black Southerners about everyday life under Jim Crow — teachers, farmers, midwives, church leaders — recorded 1990s about the 1890s-1950s.

sources.notes: One of the largest single oral-history collections of Jim Crow-era lived experience; digitized audio in the Duke Digital Repository.
